omitted.title: Sedition
omitted.note: Not carried into the BNS. BNS s.152 (acts endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India) is a new, differently worded offence. Read both texts before treating them as the same.

omitted.title: Attempt to commit suicide
omitted.note: Not carried over as a general offence. BNS s.226 is a narrower, related offence; check its text.

omitted.title: Adultery
omitted.note: Struck down by the Supreme Court in Joseph Shine v. Union of India (2018) and not carried into the BNS.

new.title: Murder by a group of five or more persons on grounds of race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language or personal belief
new.note: New provision (commonly called mob lynching). No IPC counterpart.

new.title: Terrorist act
new.note: New provision. No IPC counterpart (earlier covered by special law).

new.title: Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
new.note: New provision. Not a re-enactment of IPC s.124A; read the text.

unchanged.name: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
unchanged.note: The Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 was not repealed or renumbered by the 2023 codes. Sections 138, 139, 141, 142, 143, 143A, 145, 147 and 148 keep their numbers. What changed is the procedure the Act borrows from the criminal procedure code: summons, evidence, compounding and appeals now follow the BNSS. Rows tagged for NI Act cases show those equivalents.
